title: Give teachers their time back.
subtitle: Tanaffus · Smarter Teacher Workflow
note: AICA & AI Alliance · Case A · Working prototype and proposed business model
notes: Tanaffus means break. The prototype uses synthetic sample data and simulated analysis. We have no measured traction or production AI integration to claim.

title: The work after the school day
subtitle: The problem and the value proposition
columns: The repeated work
Checking answers, writing similar feedback, recording grades and assembling reports compete with lesson planning.
Our mission
Reduce repetitive grading and administration while keeping the teacher responsible for every academic decision.
Our vision
Teachers spend more time responding to learning needs and less time transferring information between tools.
note: Pilot hypothesis: one 28-paper assignment takes less teacher time with assisted review. This is not yet a measured result.
notes: Problem statement comes from the supplied IT Case A criteria. Baseline and savings must be validated by observation, not by the speed of this simulated demo.

title: A complete teacher-controlled workflow
subtitle: The product
columns: Prepare and analyze
Choose a class, set the rubric, and upload student work. Analysis proposes scores with evidence and confidence.
Review and approve
Trust Light separates routine papers from uncertain ones. Edit scores and feedback. Manually grade unclear work.
Report and teach
Export approved grades and feedback. Mistake Radar connects common errors to a short classroom activity.
note: The local prototype implements this journey using sample papers. No real OCR, AI grading, messaging or school sync is connected.

title: An initial market we can reach
subtitle: Uzbekistan secondary schools
body: Start with mathematics departments in Tashkent’s non-state schools. Smaller pilots let us test handwriting accuracy, willingness to pay and teacher adoption before broader procurement.
note: Official counts: start of academic year 2025/26. Non-state schools increased 21.1% year over year.
notes: National Statistics Committee, published 31 March 2026, pages 1–3. School counts are institutions, not teacher users. TAM price scenario: 11,118 × $1,080 = $12,007,440 annual revenue ceiling if every institution bought one 30-seat plan, an unrealistic upper bound rather than a forecast. SAM scenario: 551 × $1,080 = $595,080. Initial city segment: 145 × $1,080 = $156,600. National scaling requires curriculum, procurement and infrastructure validation.

title: Teachers use it. Schools sponsor it.
subtitle: Target users and adoption
columns: Primary user
Mathematics teachers in grades 8–10 who repeatedly mark short written assignments. Start with one department.
Buyer and champion
A school principal or academic coordinator pays. A lead teacher recruits colleagues and owns the pilot’s rubric.
Reason to stay
Reusable rubrics, clear teacher overrides, exportable reports and useful follow-up lessons. Measure repeat use rather than sign-ups.
note: Adoption plan: 20-minute onboarding, one assignment graded alongside the existing method, then a weekly feedback session.

title: One assignment, all the way through
subtitle: The live demo
steps: Create an assignment and choose the grading rubric.
Load 28 sample papers and watch the analysis pipeline.
Bulk approve 25 high-confidence papers. Review two uncertain papers.
Manually check the red paper, edit feedback, and approve.
Download the class report. Open Mistake Radar’s five-minute lesson.
note: Demonstration only. Time-saving illustration: 28 × (4 − 0.5) minutes = 98 minutes, excluding setup and exceptional cases.
notes: Run npm run dev and open http://127.0.0.1:5173. Reset the demo in Settings if needed. The sample class uses 25 green, 2 yellow and 1 red paper. Confidence percentages are synthetic, not calibrated probabilities.

title: A school plan with predictable costs
subtitle: Proposed monetization
columns: Free trial
30 sample or consented papers for an evaluation. No open-ended free AI usage. Conversion follows a teacher time study.
School plan · $1,080/year
30 teacher seats at an effective $3 per seat per month. Shared annual allowance: 18,000 single-page papers.
Usage and service
Optional prepaid 1,000-paper blocks at $40. Onboarding and enterprise support priced separately after pilot validation.
note: All prices are hypotheses in USD equivalents, not local quotes. Forecast excludes overages and services; willingness to pay remains untested.
notes: Pooling papers across teachers reduces unused quotas and makes school budgeting easier. Forecast assumes 30 activated seats per school, 50 papers per teacher per month, and 12 months of normalized consumption including reporting usage. Actual school seasonality must be measured. Test annual versus academic-year contracts. Full allowance yields $360 annual inference cost at $0.02 per paper; retries and multi-page papers need metering.

title: School pilots create the first reference users
subtitle: Go-to-market and expansion
columns: First 90 days
Recruit 3 schools through lead teachers and direct demos. Obtain school approval and consent before real student work.
Months 4–12
Run six-week pilots with paired manual and assisted grading. Publish consented case studies. Target 10 paid schools at year-end.
Year 2 and 3
Use teacher referrals and academic coordinator outreach. Expand across regions, then evaluate universities and neighboring language markets.
note: Illustrative Year 1 funnel: 100 qualified school contacts, 25 demos, 15 pilots, 10 paid schools. Conversion is a target, not evidence.
notes: A first pilot is three schools; later cohorts bring the annual pilot total to fifteen. No relationships, contracts, letters of intent or customer validation have been secured in this task. Partnerships and integrations remain proposed.

title: A modest scale still needs early funding
subtitle: Three-year operating scenario · USD, before tax
note: Assumptions: $1,080 per school per year; 30 seats; $0.02 per paper. Three-year operating funding gap: $82,800, before contingency.
notes: Average paid schools approximate linear ramp: (0+10)/2=5, (10+50)/2=30, (50+150)/2=100. Revenue uses average schools, not year-end schools. Papers: 90,000; 540,000; 1,800,000 (average teachers × 50 × 12). AI costs: $1,800; $10,800; $36,000. Hosting/support: $1,200; $4,800; $12,000. Product team: $27,000; $38,000; $48,000. Sales: $4,000; $10,000; $16,000. Admin: $5,000; $6,000; $8,000. These are lean founder-led cash budgets, not market salary benchmarks. No taxes, FX effects, financing costs or capital expenditure are included. Salaries and implementation costs require local quotes. $82,800 × 1.2 = $99,360 with 20% contingency.

title: Value, accuracy and retention decide expansion
subtitle: Key metrics and downside sensitivity
columns: Pilot release gates
Median teacher review time at least 50% lower, including setup. At least 95% of scores within one point of an adjudicated 20-point rubric. Zero unapproved grade transfers.
Adoption targets
70% monthly active paid teachers. 80% annual school retention. Audit corrections by language and handwriting quality. Aim for fully loaded school CAC below $600.
Cost sensitivity
At $0.04 per paper, Year 3 cost rises by $36,000 and loss reaches $48,000. Reprice limits or reduce cost before expanding. Lower retention also worsens the model.
note: All thresholds are proposed pilot targets. Teacher time and scoring agreement require measurement, including uncertainty and subgroup error rates.
notes: At Year 3 steady economics: annual revenue/school $1,080 less $360 AI, $48 hosting/support = $672 contribution, a 62.2% contribution margin. $600 CAC / $56 monthly contribution ≈ 10.7-month payback, before fixed team cost. Year 2 gross new schools with 80% retention: 50 − 8 = 42. Year 3: 150 − 40 = 110. Sales-budget-only CAC is not fully loaded and is not presented as observed CAC. Retention targets do not imply achieved outcomes.

title: Trust must survive the difficult cases
subtitle: Risks and practical responses
table: Adjudicated test set, visible evidence, teacher overrides, subgroup audits and confidence abstention
Minimize identity, school-approved storage, restricted access, audit logs, deletion schedule and legal review
Co-design rubrics, demonstrate one assignment, keep manual controls, measure actual time saved
Mark unreadable work for manual grading; resumable uploads and local drafts
Meter usage, run small pilots, use annual caps and monitor inference cost per paper
Export approved grades first; partner-approved API only after testing and explicit school authorization
note: These are production requirements and proposed controls. The demo itself uses sample data and local browser persistence.

title: The next milestone is evidence
subtitle: The pilot ask and long-term opportunity
body: Recruit three pilot schools and 30 mathematics teachers for a six-week evaluation after the secure MVP is ready.
columns: What we will measure
Time saved per assignment, rubric agreement, correction rate and continued teacher use.
What we need
School champions, consented sample work, teaching advisers and funding for the evaluated MVP.
What comes next
Expand only after a reliable local workflow earns trust. Add subjects and languages through separate evaluations.
note: Planning funding requirement: approximately $100,000 over three years including 20% contingency. Validate salaries, pricing and unit costs first.
